# A project as a file

One side writes a project out, the other reads it in after reading what it holds. The file is a copy of the project at one moment. Nothing links the two afterwards: a change on one side does not reach the other. A template is the same file with `template` set.

The file is JSON. It begins `{ "aubergine": "project", "format": 1, … }`.

## What a file never holds

- Anything that ran: tasks, what was written on the owner's list, runs and their notes, the log of notes (only the pinned note is in the file), messages.
- Any credential or setting: no token, nothing from the settings file.
- Anything of the computer it was written on: no path, no user name, no data folder, no working copy, no ID. Folders are written as named places, and things inside the file point at each other by references of the file's own (`c1`, `t3`, `e2`). Reading a file in makes new IDs.
- What a terminal showed or did: no screen, no scroll-back, no history, no conversation, no command line.

## Reading a file in

- Nothing is made until the owner has read what the file holds and accepted exactly that text.
- Where each place is on this computer is asked, or left unset. No path from a file is ever used as a path. A terminal with no place starts in the home folder.
- No shell is started unless the owner asks for it, and an agent never is: a terminal that was an agent's is made as a plain shell and says which agent it was meant for.
- Schedules and rules arrive switched off. Tasks start only when the owner starts them.
- A file that is wrong in any way is refused with a sentence, and nothing of it is used.

## The file

| Field | What it is |
|---|---|
| `aubergine` | Says what kind of file this is. |
| `format` | The format of the file. This version writes and reads 1; a later one is refused with a sentence. |
| `template` | True for a template: a project to start others from. |
| `description` | What it is for, in a few sentences. Shown before it is read in. |
| `name` | The name of the project. Whoever reads the file in may choose another. |
| `color` | Its color. |
| `labels` | Pairs of key and value. |
| `places` | The project's folders, as names. Where each is on a computer is asked there. |
| `canvases` | Its canvases, in the order of their tabs. At least one. |
| `workflows` | The workflows it owns and the shared ones its schedules run. Each has a reference (`w1`), `shared` (true if it was shared with every project where the file was written) and `file`: the workflow as a workflow file. |
| `elements` | The shelf elements it owns and the shared ones its rules and schedules run. Each has a reference (`e1`), `shared` and `element` (see the element reference). |
| `rules` | Its rules. |
| `schedules` | Its schedules. |
| `leftOut` | What could not be written into the file, each in a sentence. |

Fields this version does not know are kept when a file is read in, and written out again when that project is written to a file.

## A place

| Field | What it is |
|---|---|
| `name` | The name of the place: a word, such as `main` or `docs`. Terminals name it. |
| `hint` | The last part of the folder's path where the file was written, to help whoever is asked where the place is. Never used as a path. |
| `default` | True for the place new terminals start in. |

## A canvas

| Field | What it is |
|---|---|
| `ref` | Its reference inside this file, such as `c1`. |
| `name` | The name on its tab. |
| `color` | The color of its tab. |
| `labels` | Pairs of key and value. |
| `frames` | Its frames: a rectangle, a label and a color each. |
| `nodes` | Its nodes, in the order they are drawn: a rectangle, a color, and the terminal to make there. |

## A terminal, on a node

| Field | What it is |
|---|---|
| `ref` | Its reference inside this file, such as `t1`. Rules and schedules name it. |
| `name` | What the terminal is called. |
| `tags` | Its tags. |
| `note` | Its pinned note. Left out of a template unless the owner kept the notes. |
| `place` | The place it starts in. Null: no place; it starts in the home folder of whoever reads the file in. |
| `subfolder` | A folder below that place. |
| `agent` | The agent it ran, by its kind. It is made as a plain shell and says which agent it was meant for: reading a file in never starts an agent. |
| `environment` | The kind of place it worked in. Said on the terminal; nothing is prepared by reading the file in. |

## A rule

| Field | What it is |
|---|---|
| `event` | What sets it off. |
| `action` | What it does: `{"kind":"notify"}`, or `{"kind":"run-element","element":"e1","on":{"terminal":"t1"}}` (or `{"canvas":"c1"}` for a new terminal there). It arrives switched off. |

## A schedule

| Field | What it is |
|---|---|
| `name` | What the schedule is called. It arrives switched off. |
| `time` | The time of day, on this computer's clock and in its time zone. |
| `days` | The days of the week it runs on. |
| `what` | What it runs: `{"element":"e1"}` or `{"workflow":"w1"}`. |
| `where` | Where: `{"terminal":"t1"}`, or `{"canvas":"c1"}` for a new terminal there. |
| `task` | What the agent is told to do. |

## Bounds

A file is at most 400000 characters. It may hold 50 canvases, 200 nodes and 100 frames on a canvas, 300 terminals in all, 20 places, 50 workflows, 100 elements, 50 rules and 50 schedules.
